topology: real C++ sink -> private intents -> separate C++ Sport guard -> simulated controller
authority: Trusted ArbiterStatus protocol stand-in plus explicit guard instance/protection/readiness token; complete native recovery integration not tested.

fake_go2_cases.unprotected_sink_sigkill: simulated vx > 0.15 m/s beyond 1.1 seconds after kill
fake_go2_cases.guarded_sink_sigkill: independent repeated StopMove; simulated vx < 0.01 m/s; latch retained through sink restart

other_controller_model: Retains last Move target indefinitely; StopMove can be accepted, denied or dropped.
authorization_regressions: Old held/released status pair cannot automatically reopen a restarted guard.
Old guard instance token is rejected.
Same-instance prehealth token delivered after readiness is rejected.
Request/status gaps invalidate ready authorization before incoming timestamp refresh.
Current explicit authorization succeeds after continuous current readiness.
acknowledgment: Positive forwarded sink IDs and shared controller response preserve sink matching; negative IDs track guard Stops. Guard telemetry always reports measured_stopped=false.
observed_remaining_failures: Unprotected native sink death has no surviving controller stop sender.
Guard death leaves persistent simulated motion.
Denied or dropped StopMove leaves persistent simulated motion.
limitations: No physical GO2 stop-on-command-silence contract or measurement.
No protection established against common host, power, DDS or network failure.
Competing controller publishers and actuator/controller failure are outside the guarantee.
Receipt ordering cannot establish emission age of unseen queued messages; protocol is not authenticated.
Lower request IDs after restart fail closed, limiting availability.
reproduce: source install/setup.bash; ROS_LOCALHOST_ONLY=1 python3 -m pytest tests/sim_integration/test_sport_guard.py -q
